title: Canonical pullback comparisons intertwine coefficient-map iterates
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $h:W\to X$ a morphism of schemes, and $t:X\to X$, $t_W:W\to W$ endomorphisms with $ht_W=th$. Use ordinary derived categories of constant $A$-module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, with exact inverse images $Lf^*=f^{-1}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $P_m=L(t^m)^*$ and $Q_m=L(t_W^m)^*$ for $m\geq0$, using the identity comparisons at $m=0$. Let $d^X_m:P_{m+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1P_m$ and $d^W_m:Q_{m+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_1Q_m$ be the canonical pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Write $c_m:Q_mLh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*P_m$ for the comparison obtained from $ht_W^m=t^mh$. For every derived complex $K$, these canonical comparisons satisfy
$$Lh^*(d^X_{m,K})\circ c_{m+1,K}=c_{1,P_mK}\circ Q_1(c_{m,K})\circ d^W_{m,Lh^*K}\quad(m\geq0).$$
For any morphism $u:P_1K\to K$, define $u_1=u$ and $u_{m+1}=u\circ P_1(u_m)\circ d^X_{m,K}$. Put $v=Lh^*(u)\circ c_{1,K}$ and define $v_m$ by the same recursion with $Q_m,d^W_m$. Then
$$v_m=Lh^*(u_m)\circ c_{m,K}\quad(m\geq1).$$
No invertibility, finite-type or Cartesian-square hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Work first with ordinary $A$-module sheaves. For composable scheme maps $f:S\to T$, $g:T\to V$, the direct-image formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies $(gf)_*$ with $g_*f_*$ by the canonical isomorphism $S\times_V B\cong S\times_T(T\times_V B)$, for each pro-etale $B\to V$. Both maps of a threefold fibre product to the single fibre product preserve the projection to $S$ and the projection to $B$; hence they agree by the fibre-product universal property. The identity comparisons have the same property. Thus these direct-image comparisons are associative and unital. They are module-linear: the constant-ring structure maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] send a constant $a$ to the same $a$ on every base-changed object, so both composite ring actions agree. This also checks that the coefficient identification for a composite is the composite coefficient identification, rather than an independently chosen automorphism of $A$.

source.place: Tag 03D8, label lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; direct-image formula and fibre-product universal property

proof.text: Write $F_f=f^*$ on module sheaves and $R_f=f_*$. Use the adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] has unit $R_g(\eta_{f,F_gM})\circ\eta_{g,M}$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with the direct-image comparison of Step 1 gives a unique natural isomorphism $a_{f,g}:F_{gf}\to F_fF_g$ carrying $\eta_{gf}$ to this composite unit (with the right-adjoint comparison inserted). This is the ordinary canonical module-pullback comparison: successive adjunctions identify maps out of $F_fF_gM$ with maps out of $M$ into $R_gR_f$, and the comparison identifies the latter with $R_{gf}$. Equivalently, in the inverse-image/tensor presentation it sends $m\otimes r$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes r$ after the inverse-image identification; the inverse multiplies the two scalar factors, using the coefficient identification. The balancing relation shows the two composites are identities. Under adjunction both maps carry $m$ to its two successive unit images, verifying the stated normalization.

source.place: Tag 03D8, label lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; categories.tex Tags 0B65 and 0DV0 for the adjunction normalization

proof.text:
For three composable maps $f,g,k$, both composites from $F_{kgf}$ to $F_fF_gF_k$ carry its unit, under the direct-image identifications of Step 1, to
$$R_kR_g(\eta_fF_gF_k)\circ R_k(\eta_gF_k)\circ\eta_k.$$
Indeed expand the composite unit twice using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; reassociation gives exactly these three factors, and naturality moves each comparison through the next unit. The right-adjoint identifications agree by Step 1. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] therefore gives
$$F_f(a_{g,k})\circ a_{f,kg}=(a_{f,g}F_k)\circ a_{gf,k}.$$
For an identity map, the same unit equation has the identity transformation as its solution after the identity adjunction identification, proving the unit laws. These are equalities of natural transformations on all module sheaves, not just on constant sheaves.

Each $F_f$ is exact and $Lf^*$ is induced by its termwise action, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) to the termwise natural isomorphisms $a_{f,g}$ and the identity comparisons; the termwise functors invert quasi-isomorphisms because they are exact. The same node says descent respects composition and is faithful on natural transformations, so the associativity and unit identities of Step 3 descend to the ordinary unbounded derived categories. These descended comparisons are the comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]: choose for any complex a K-flat resolution with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. On that resolution both comparisons are the class of the same termwise canonical module-pullback map, exactly the normalization in the cited binary-composition statement. Naturality along the resolution quasi-isomorphism, whose image is invertible under all these exact functors, gives equality at the original complex. Henceforth write $F_f=Lf^*$ and use $a$ for these derived comparisons.

proof.text:
Put $H=Lh^*$, $T=t_W$ and continue to write $a_{f,g}:L(gf)^*\to Lf^*Lg^*$. The equality $hT^m=t^mh$ follows by induction from $hT=th$. By the definition of the canonical square comparison,
$$c_m=a_{h,t^m}\circ a_{T^m,h}^{-1},\quad d^X_m=a_{t,t^m},\quad d^W_m=a_{T,T^m}.$$
Step 4's associativity, for the triples $(h,t,t^m)$, $(T,h,t^m)$ and $(T,T^m,h)$, respectively, reads
$$H(a_{t,t^m})a_{h,t^{m+1}}=(a_{h,t}P_m)a_{th,t^m},$$
$$Q_1(a_{h,t^m})a_{T,t^mh}=(a_{T,h}P_m)a_{hT,t^m},$$
$$Q_1(a_{T^m,h})a_{T,hT^m}=(a_{T,T^m}H)a_{T^{m+1},h}.$$
Here juxtaposition denotes composition, rightmost factor first. Substitute $th=hT$ and $t^mh=hT^m$; eliminate $a_{hT,t^m}$ with the second equality and $a_{T,hT^m}$ with the third. Multiplying on the right by $a_{T^{m+1},h}^{-1}$ gives precisely
$$H(d^X_m)c_{m+1}=(c_1P_m)Q_1(c_m)d^W_m.$$
This calculation is valid also at $m=0$, using the unit laws of Step 4.

source.place: Step 1, the pullback-identification cocycle, written as three associativity equations; Step 6 for noninvertible coefficient maps

proof.text:
Induct on $m\geq1$ on the assertion $v_m=H(u_m)c_{m,K}$. For $m=1$ this is the definition $v=H(u)c_{1,K}$. For the induction step use functoriality of $Q_1$ and the induction hypothesis in the recursion:
$$v_{m+1}=H(u)c_{1,K}\,Q_1(H(u_m))\,Q_1(c_{m,K})\,d^W_{m,HK}.$$
Naturality of $c_1:Q_1H\to HP_1$ for the derived morphism $u_m:P_mK\to K$ gives
$$c_{1,K}Q_1(H(u_m))=H(P_1(u_m))c_{1,P_mK}.$$
Replace this pair of factors and use Step 5 for the three remaining comparison factors. Functoriality of $H$ now gives
$$v_{m+1}=H(u)H(P_1(u_m))H(d^X_{m,K})c_{m+1,K}=H(u_{m+1})c_{m+1,K}.$$
This uses naturality for arbitrary derived morphisms, not a choice of a chain representative of $u$. None of the argument in Steps 1–6 uses an inverse of $u$, a finite-type hypothesis on the schemes, or a Cartesian hypothesis on the commuting square.
